subject: Quantaforge Dedicated: surge lanes & autoscale amendment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Feldman <nora@quantaforge.com>, Quantaforge Procurement <purchases@quantaforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantaforge Dedicated: proposal for surge lanes and autoscale terms

Hi Nora / team,

Thanks again for the workshop last week — great alignment on expected production patterns. Attached is a concise term sheet describing the Dedicated baseline we discussed plus the proposed surge lanes (we're calling them "elastic buffer lanes") and the autoscale policy we think fits Quantaforge's workload. High-level summary:  

- Baseline Reserved: 8 GPUs (pinned to your dedicated pool)
- Elastic buffer lanes: up to 16 additional GPUs for short spikes (3-hour daily window as a default)
- Credit model: burst usage is accounted via monthly credits; unused credits do not roll over
- Warmup & ramp: 2-minute soft ramp with a 60s preemption window for preemptible nodes

Key asks from our side before we finalize: a short confirmation on acceptable daily spike window, whether you need capped dollar exposure during bursts, and any procurement/PO constraints for a 12-month amendment. I've attached the term sheet and a draft amendment we can iterate on.

If this looks reasonable, propose a 30-min sync with your CloudOps and procurement tomorrow to walk the economics line-by-line.

Attachments: 20290514_qf-burst_term_sheet.pdf

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Nora Feldman <nora@quantaforge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quantaforge Dedicated: proposal for surge lanes and autoscale terms

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions before we loop procurement:  

1) Billing during bursts — is it billed as consumed GPU-hours at a higher "burst" rate, or do we draw from an upfront credit bucket?
2) Eviction behavior — for jobs that are long-running (90–120s per request in our bench), what guarantees do we have about partial work and retries when preemption occurs?
3) Auditability — procurement will want event logs showing when burst capacity is allocated and which requests were routed to elastic lanes.

We prefer a capped daily dollar exposure (upper bound) if possible — can you provide a notional example of monthly costs under the expected traffic profile?

Happy to take the 30-min sync; will invite CloudOps and procurement if you share a proposed slot.

Best,
Nora Feldman
CTO, Quantaforge
Nora.Feldman@quantaforge.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Feldman <nora@quantaforge.com>, Quantaforge Procurement <purchases@quantaforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 13:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantaforge Dedicated: proposal for surge lanes and autoscale terms

Hi Nora — quick answers inline and a proposed commercial model.

Billing model: we support both. For the proposed plan we recommend a credit-bucket amortization (simpler for forecasting) but will provide an on-demand metered rate if you prefer pay-as-you-go. Example: we issue 9,600 burst credits/month (equivalent to ~160 GPU-hours); each GPU-minute of burst consumes 1 credit; additional credits billed at $1.90/credit.

Eviction/partial work: preemptible nodes are drained with a 60s preemption window. For requests that exceed the window we recommend enabling automatic retry routing to the baseline pool or fallback to a quantized model variant — this reduces waste and maintains latency targets. We'll provide request-level retry headers and unique attempt IDs so you can reconcile at your side.

Auditability: we will include burst-allocation events in the audit log (timestamped), plus per-request routing traces for 90 days (longer retention is an add-on).

I've attached a draft amendment that maps the credit model to contract terms. If procurement prefers capped daily spend, we can map a hard stop to the credit-bucket and notify you at 80% and 95% thresholds.

Attachments: qf-burst_amendment_v0.docx

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Quantaforge Procurement <purchases@quantaforge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Feldman <nora@quantaforge.com>, CloudOps <ops@quantaforge.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 09:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quantaforge Dedicated: proposal for surge lanes and autoscale terms

Team,

Thanks for the clarity. Procurement has redlines on the draft amendment:  

- Require a daily hard cap (we propose $3,500/day) that prevents burst spend above this without explicit PO amendment.
- Notification SLA: email + webhook at 80%/95% burn thresholds within 5 minutes.
- Audit logs: retain burst allocation and per-request routing traces for 12 months for compliance review.
- Data handling: any request routed to elastic lanes must adhere to our data residency rule (no egress outside US).

I've attached the redline PDF with inline comments. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these or propose edits.

Attachments: quantaforge_redline_contract.pdf

Regards,
Quantaforge Procurement
procurement@quantaforge.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Quantaforge Procurement <purchases@quantaforge.com>, Nora Feldman <nora@quantaforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantaforge Dedicated: proposal for surge lanes and autoscale terms

Hi all — technical response to the redlines and a feasibility note.  

- Daily hard cap: can be implemented by converting the credit-bucket into a hard-stop. We'll emit an account-level kill switch event and block new elastic allocations once the cap is hit, while allowing in-flight requests to drain according to the preemption window.
- Notifications: we can emit webhook events and email alerts at 80/95% within ~2 minutes; 5 minutes is fine as a contractual SLA.
- Audit logs: we can extend retention to 12 months for burst allocation events and per-request routing metadata. This will add a minor storage uplift; I'll capture the estimated delta in INFRA-7821.
- Data residency: we will pin elastic lanes serving Quantaforge to the US region only. No egress outside US.

Operational mitigations we recommend: pre-warmed hot path (warm containers kept idle) to reduce warmup to ~45s instead of 2 minutes for critical endpoints, plus a "graceful downgrade" to a quantized model variant when almost out of credits to avoid failed requests. We'll open a small Jira to track the infra changes: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-7821

Let us know if procurement wants the daily cap enforced as a hard automated stop or as a soft throttle + human approval.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Quantaforge Procurement <purchases@quantaforge.com>, Nora Feldman <nora@quantaforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quantaforge Dedicated: surge lanes & autoscale amendment — next steps

Thanks everyone — good progress. Next steps I propose:  

1) Internal decision: Redwood accepts the 12-month audit retention and US-only elastic lanes. Requesting internal approval on the $3,500/day hard cap implementation vs soft throttle. Ben — can you run the pricing impact and advise if we accept the cap as-is or propose $2,800/day?
2) Engineering commit: Karthik to scope INFRA-7821 for warm-path pre-warming and credit hard-stop behavior. Ops: provide ETA for rollout.
3) Procurement: once we align on the cap and retention, I'll circulate an updated amendment via DocuSign for signature (DocuSign link will be included).

Please reply with approvals or objections; if no objections by Monday EOD I'll schedule the 30-min sync with Quantaforge CloudOps and Procurement to finalize remaining commercial points.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
